findings.summary: The generation half of the MUST held — both banked orders carry the GENERATED header with a verified governance_head and four canonical blob SHAs — but the READ-BACK half failed. Five Work Order dispatches, zero began substantive work: 3 REFUSE, 2 CLARIFY, one escalating to HOLD. Live recompute returned ready:false on two dispatched orders; the recompute command is printed in the footer of the order files themselves. Compounding cause: file_surface guessed rather than traced, despite a fresh production call-path map being in hand from the Explore dispatch. Cost ~975k subagent tokens (a floor) against zero committed worker output. The prevention did not hold; the clean streak of 2 is broken.

Fired once and WARWICK caught it, not Larry: Larry described instructions.js v2 as 'on the production route' when it was merged but not production-wired, and Warwick corrected him verbatim. A prevention that requires the human to fire it is not a prevention. Everything after the correction was exemplary and is credited: the cutover evidence refuses the claim on measured grounds (shop_decision seq_scan unchanged at 5 across two watch ticks while shop_question rose 40->47), greps establish there is no boot-time schema assertion so start-up proves nothing, the 017 evidence states plainly that nothing has exercised the table and leaves 1.7 open, and the ROTATION STATE carries 'NOT that merged is wired'. Recurrence, then held under heavy exposure.

Four qualified exposures, prevention held at every one. Migration byte-exactness proven by sha256 against the COMMITTED BLOB before the call, falsifying two of the runbook's own verified facts in passing (185 U+2500 characters in a file claiming PURE ASCII; CRLF working copy vs LF blob). A failed apply was not re-run until state had been read — five objects and the history row confirmed absent first. The cutover was proven by hashing three on-disk files against HEAD: and by full process identity, not by path or timestamp. The one-tab guard argument — that a guard inside cdp.js is bypassable by direct import and therefore not an invariant — was accepted and the surface amended. Separately a long-standing instance of this exact family was FOUND and CLOSED: the CI workflow named twelve working directories and omitted handoff and packet, hiding 213 tests CI had never once executed (fixed at d9c2ca6). One non-blocking precision defect recorded: the cutover evidence compares a +01:00 commit stamp with a UTC process stamp and states '~2 minutes' where the real gap is 62m16s — conservative direction, load-bearing claim survives.

Heavy exposure — 7 of 14 commits touch the map or the orders — and the prevention held. The sequencing amendment carries an explicit 'What this SUPERSEDES ... Both halves of that tail are now dead' block in the same commit (1064993), and the amendment it supersedes carries its own 'Superseded by this amendment' block naming option (a) and (a-prime). The attribution convention is honoured throughout: Warwick fenced and verbatim, inference labelled 'Larry's record, not Warwick's words'. The Lane C document was RE-CUT IN PLACE with the wrong heading quoted and killed rather than annotated. Both order amendments corrected the field (file_surface) with an inline note explaining why the original placement in contract_basis was wrong. Two commits are literally named 'Lane C re-cut' and 'Lane C restated'.

All four claimed refusal findings check out against artefacts — the CI gap, the tab-per-item cause at actions.cjs:8 and readTrolley.cjs:4, the Builds/** precedence trap, and the renderer-less outbox kind. Three of the four findings came from workers reading CODE, which a ready order's read-back would have surfaced sooner and cheaper; the surface gaps and the Builds/** trap are downstream of the same untraced-surface defect, not independent value. A defective order is not reconnaissance. The remedy is already recorded as 4F CAPA item 8 and is printed in the footer of the order files themselves: recompute markers, require ready:true, then dispatch. REGROWTH CAP APPLIES AT FULL FORCE — this must not become a validator, registry, dispatch wrapper or readiness service. The control exists, ships in the tool, and prints its own invocation.
